subject: dsa
title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
summary: Merging keeps the larger value in each position, so a triplet is usable only if no value exceeds the target. If the column-wise max over the usable triplets equals the target, it is achievable.
problem: Merging two triplets keeps the element-wise maximum; decide if some sequence of merges can produce the target triplet.

steps.caption: Merging two triplets keeps the larger value in each spot. Reach the target [2,7,5] using only triplets that never exceed it.
Row 0 is [2,5,3]: every value is <= the target [2,7,5], so this triplet is usable.
Row 1 is [1,8,4]: its middle value 8 > 7, so it is rejected. Using it would overshoot that position forever.
Row 2 is [1,7,5]: all values are <= the target, so it is usable too.
Now take the column-wise max of the usable rows 0 and 2. Column 0: max(2, 1) = 2, supplied by row 0.
Column 1: max(5, 7) = 7 from row 2. Column 2: max(3, 5) = 5 from row 2. The usable rows combine to [2,7,5].
The merged maxima equal the target [2,7,5], so it is achievable. Answer: true.
